title: Reading a Science Article I: Claim, Method, Sample Size
goal: Learn to pull apart a science write-up into its actual claim, the method used to test it, and the sample size — and notice when a headline overstates what the study behind it found.

questions: State the article's actual claim (not the headline) in one sentence: what, precisely, changed, by how much, for whom?
What was the method? Name at least two things about the method that are weaker than they'd need to be to support "proves" in the company's own words.
What was the sample size, and name one specific reason (given in the article) that this sample might not represent "teenagers today" in general.
